questions.q:
As shown in the figure, after passing through the medium $1$.~The speed of light ${v}_{2}$ in medium $2$ will be :
(Given $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The refractive index of a medium is given by,& $n = \sqrt{{μ}_{r}{ε}_{r}}$.

For medium~$2$,~${n}_{2} = \sqrt{1 \times 9} = 3$

Now speed of light in a medium will be,

$\dfrac{c}{v} = n ⇒ v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3} = 1 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A plano - convex lens (focal length ${f}_{2}$ , refractive index ${\mu}_{2},$ radius of curvature R) fits exactly into a plano - concave lens (focal length ${f}_{1},$ refractive index ${\mu}_{1},$ radius of curvature R). Their plane surfaces are parallel to each other. Then, the focal length of the combination will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{- R} - \dfrac{1}{\omega}\right)\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} =\left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\omega}\right)

When joined together

\dfrac{1}{{f}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{- R} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{R} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}

$⇒ {f}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}

$\delta=$\mathrm{I}$+\mathrm{e}-\mathrm{A}$

questions.q: Car $B$ overtakes another car $A$ at a relative speed of $40\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. How fast will the image of car $B$ appear to move in the mirror of focal length $10$ cm fitted in car $A$, when the car $B$ is $1 . 9m$ away from the car $A$?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Object distance,& $u = - 1.9m = 190cm$

Focal length,~$f = 10cm$

Magnification,~$m = \dfrac{f}{f - u} = \dfrac{10}{10 - ( - 190 )}$

Therefore,~$m = \dfrac{10}{200} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

Image velocity,~${V}_{I} = - m^{2}{V}_{0} = - \left(\dfrac{1}{20}\right)2 \times 40$

Hence,~${V}_{I} = - 0.1ms^{- 1}$

Magnitude of velocity~$= 0 . 1ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: An ice cube has a bubble inside. When viewed from one side the apparent distance of the bubble is $12$ cm. When viewed from the opposite side, the apparent distance of the bubble is observed as $4$ cm. If the side of the ice cube is $24$ cm, the refractive index of the ice cube is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's assume that the original position of the bubble is& $x$~from one side of the ice cube of side~$a$.

When the bubble is seen from one side, it can be written that

$\dfrac{x}{μ} = 12 . . . \left(1\right)$

For the view from the other side, it can be written that

\dfrac{a - x}{μ} =$4 . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it is given that

$\begin{cases}24 - 12\mu & = & 4\mu \\ & ⇒ & \mu = \dfrac{24}{16}\\ & = & 1 . 5\end{cases}$

questions.q: A mirror is used to produce an image with magnification of $\frac{1}{4}$. If the distance between object and its image is 40 cm , then the focal length of the mirror is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=-\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=-\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}}{-\mathrm{u}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}} \\ & \frac{1}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=4 \mathrm{v} \\ & \mathrm{v}+\mathrm{u}=40 \\ & 5 \mathrm{v}=40 \\ & \mathrm{v}=8 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \mathrm{u}=32 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{32}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{4-1}{32}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \mathrm{f}=\frac{32}{3}=10.7 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A transparent film of refractive index, 2.0 is coated on a glass slab of refractive index, 1.45. What is the minimum thickness of transparent film to be coated for the maximum transmission of Green light of wavelength 550 nm . [Assume that the light is incident nearly perpendicular to the glass surface.]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: For transmitted green light to be maxima, reflected green should be minima. $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{P}=2 \mu_0 \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n} \lambda \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{n} \lambda}{2 \mu_0} \therefore \mathrm{t}_{\min }=\frac{\lambda}{2 \mu_0}=\frac{550}{2 \times 2}=137.5 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A biconvex lens of refractive index $1 . 5$ has a focal length of $20$ cm in air. Its focal length when immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1 . 6$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the refractive index of the material of the lens is ${μ}_{1} = 1 . 5$, the refractive index of the medium is ${μ}_{m} = 1 . 6$ and the focal length of the lens in air is ${f}_{a} = 20cm$.

In air:

$\dfrac{1}{fa} = \left({μ}_{1} -$1\right)\left[\dfrac{2}{R}\right]

In liquid:

\dfrac{1}{fm} =\left(\dfrac{\mu1}{\mum} -1\right)\left[\dfrac{2}{R}\right]

The focal length as measured in air and that as measured inside the liquid medium are related by,

\dfrac{fm}{fa} = \left({μ}_{1} -1\right){μ}_{m} \left({μ}_{1} - {μ}_{m}\right) . . . \left($1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

$\dfrac{fm}{20} = \dfrac{( 1 . 5 - 1 ) 1 . 6}{( 1 . 5 - 1 . 6 )}⇒ {f}_{m} = - 160cm

$

So, distance of object from mirror$= 0.32m$

questions.q: For a concave lens of focal length $f$, the relation between object and image distance $u$ and $v,$ respectively, from its pole can best be represented by ($u = v$ is the reference line):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the lens formula,& $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ v = f - \dfrac{f2}{u + f}$

~now, if we plot a graph between~$u\text{and}v$

When~$u \to \infty ; v = f - \dfrac{f2}{∞} = f$

and for~$u \to 0; v = 0$

Given that~$u = v$is~a reference line, therefore,~$\dfrac{d v}{d u} = 0 + \dfrac{f2}{\left(u + f\right)2}$

${\dfrac{d v}{d u}}_{u = 0} = 0 + \dfrac{f2}{\left(0 + f\right)2} = 1$

The equation of tangent of the curve at the origin,~$v - 0 = 1\left(u - 0\right) ⇒ v = u$

questions.q: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is :

questions.solution:
For Convex mirror
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{30} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{2}{30}=\frac{1}{15} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=15 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Image formed by convex mirror is at 45 cm from object so plane mirror should be placed midway at 22.5 cm from object so that both of their images may coinside,
Therefore distance between both mirrors
$=30-22.5=7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$
Correct Answer : Option 2

Statement (I) : When an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave lens, image is formed at the centre of curvature of the lens on the other side.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-2 \mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{-\mathrm{f}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{-1}{2 \mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=-2 \mathrm{f} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \text { Virtual image of Real object. }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In an experiment with a convex lens. The plot of the image distance  \left(v^{'}\right)$ against the object distance  \left({μ}^{'}\right)$ measured from the focus gives a curve $v^{'}{μ}^{'} = 225$. If all the distances are measured in $cm$. The magnitude of the focal length of the lens is _____~$cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Newton's formula for lenses,

$vu = f^{2}$~, here,~$f$~is focal length of the lens.

Given here,~$v^{'}{μ}^{'} = 225$

Thus, focal length of the lens is~$f^{2} = 225$

Or~$f = 15cm$

questions.q: Two convex lenses of focal length $20$ cm each are placed coaxially with a separation of $60$ cm~between them. The image of the distant object formed by the combination is at _____ $cm$& from the first lens.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${L}_{1}$~be the first lens and~${L}_{2}$~be the second lens.

The first refraction is in~${L}_{1}$.

Using lens formula,

${u}_{1} = \infty , {f}_{1} = 20cm, \dfrac{1}{v1} - 0 = \dfrac{1}{f1} ⇒ {v}_{1} = 20cm$

Hence, the distance between the second image and the~${L}_{2}$~would be~\left(60 - 20\right) = 40cm$.

For the second lens~${L}_{2}$,

${u}_{2} = - 40cm, {f}_{2} = 20cm, \dfrac{1}{v2} - \dfrac{1}{u2} = \dfrac{1}{f2} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{v2} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{v2} = \dfrac{1}{40} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 40cm$

So, the distance of image from first lens is

$x = 40cm + 60cm$

$= 100cm$

$

questions.q:
A prism of angle& $A = 1 °\mu = 1 . 5$. A good estimate for the minimum angle of deviation (in degrees) is close to $\dfrac{N}{10} .$ Value of $N$~is~$\ldots \ldots \ldots$
&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Angle of prism,& $A = 1 °$

Refractive index of prism,~$\mu = 1 . 5$

For this prism, minimum angle of deviation is given by

$\delta = ( \mu - 1 ) A$

$⇒ \delta = ( 1 . 5 - 1 ) \times 1 ° = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{N}{10}$

$⇒ N = 5$
